title: The Crescent Beneath Falling Snow
text:
The black jade tablet from the northern archive did not open for three days.

The name needed context even in the northern archive.

Jiang Taixuan was not one of the Top Ten. He held no Duke or Marquise title and had never submitted himself to the modern ranking system. Far beyond the northern passes, however, stories called him the **Uncrowned Emperor** — an unranked martial sovereign who had defeated every challenger offered to him and built the Black Sun Host around his authority.

Sera had never met him.

Neither had Rhen.

That made the fresh ink beside his name considerably worse.

On the fourth morning, Sera found Rhen already awake.

He was sitting at the tea-shop table with the tablet in front of him.

No tea.

That worried her more than the tablet.

[[speaker:sera]]“You know the symbol.”

Rhen nodded.

A crescent beneath falling snow.

[[speaker:rhen]]“It belonged to a martial state beyond the northern passes.”

[[speaker:sera]]“Belonged?”

[[speaker:rhen]]“It disappeared.”

Sera sat beside him.

Closer than necessary.

That had become normal.

The archive finally opened at noon.

Inside lay maps extending far beyond every modern border, together with a single recent report written in fresh ink.

BLACK SUN HOST — MOVING SOUTH.

At the bottom sat one name.

JIANG TAIXUAN.

Rhen's eyes narrowed.

Sera noticed.

[[speaker:sera]]“Friend?”

[[speaker:rhen]]“No.”

[[speaker:sera]]“Enemy?”

[[speaker:rhen]]“Never met him.”

That answer surprised her.

A messenger arrived before she could ask more.

The seal belonged to World Rank #4.

Lei Zhen — Duke of the Black Storm, former World #2, and one of the youngest people ever to enter the Five Dukes.

Sera had already seen what happened when Lei fought seriously. In their earlier clash, Liang Yue had turned an empty plateau with him into a broken field of thunder.

The message contained only six words.

THE NORTH GATE HAS BEEN ATTACKED.

Sera stood.

Rhen reached for his coat.

She caught his wrist.

[[speaker:sera]]“Before we go.”

He looked at her.

Sera took one breath.

[[speaker:sera]]“You never asked properly.”

Rhen froze.

She smiled.

[[speaker:sera]]“So I'm solving that problem too.”

Then she kissed him.

Not his cheek.

Not the corner of his mouth.

Properly.

When she pulled back, Rhen looked more stunned than he had against any Duke.

[[speaker:sera]]“Rhen.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“Yes?”

[[speaker:sera]]“Marry me.”

For once in his impossible life, Rhen had absolutely nothing clever to say.

Before they left, Sera wrapped the black jade tablet in cloth and hid it beneath the tea counter. Rhen watched her choose the hiding place.

[[speaker:rhen]]“That is where you keep the expensive leaves.”

[[speaker:sera]]“Exactly. Nobody touches them.”

He considered the logic and nodded.

On the road north, Sera caught him looking at her three separate times.

[[speaker:sera]]“What?”

[[speaker:rhen]]“Nothing.”

[[speaker:sera]]“You said yes and became suspicious.”

Rhen smiled.

Sera reached across the saddle gap and touched his hand.

The northern wind was bitter. Her fingers were cold. His were warm.

For the next mile, neither mentioned the archive.

title: The Duke of the Black Storm
text:
Lei Zhen met them at the northern gate beneath a sky split by old lightning.

Lei Zhen needed little introduction in the north. **World Rank #4, Duke of the Black Storm**, he was the young thunder sovereign who had once held #2 and whose earlier clash with Liang Yue had torn apart a plateau. Brilliant, suspicious and difficult, he was one of the Five Dukes who had actually seen Rhen's face.

World Rank #4 looked younger than the devastation around him suggested.

Twenty-six.

Dark-eyed.

Sharp.

Too calm.

Sera had once known him mainly through reputation: former #2, architect of Jian Ruo's political fall, and a man dangerous enough that even other Dukes treated his preparation seriously.

Now half his fortress wall was gone.

Lei pointed toward the crater.

[[speaker:lei]]“One strike.”

Sera looked at him.

[[speaker:sera]]“From who?”

[[speaker:lei]]“Not who.”

He handed her a black iron disc.

The emblem was a sun with nine broken rays.

[[speaker:lei]]“An advance commander.”

Rhen turned the disc over.

The internal qi residue was dense, disciplined, and unfamiliar.

A second messenger ran in.

The northern ridge had fallen.

Lei moved before anyone else.

Sera followed.

Rhen followed Sera.

At the ridge they met Duan He.

The man wore lamellar armor without rank markings and carried twelve short throwing spears across his back.

He introduced himself while standing on the remains of a watchtower.

[[speaker:duan]]“Duan He. Iron Rain General of the Black Sun Host.”

He was not Duke-level.

Around the upper Marquis range.

But his battlefield system was dangerous.

**Twelve Returning Spears**.

Every spear carried a different qi route. Once thrown, the weapon did not curve magically; hidden silk-steel lines, terrain anchors and controlled recoil allowed Duan to create attack angles that seemed impossible until one saw the machinery underneath.

Lei looked at the setup once.

Thunder moved.

Duan's first six spears shattered.

His smile vanished.

[[speaker:lei]]“You attacked my gate.”

Black lightning crawled across the stone.

[[speaker:lei]]“That was impolite.”

Duan retreated before Lei could finish the lesson.

Sera watched the speed of that retreat.

Not fear.

Timing.

Someone farther north had ordered the Black Sun Host to provoke #4 and leave.

They were measuring Dukes again.

But this time the hand behind it was new.

Lei walked Sera through the damaged gate after Duan withdrew. The walls were layered with old thunder wards and newer civilian shelters beneath them.

[[speaker:lei]]“He struck here because this is where my soldiers would gather.”

Sera crouched beside a blackened stone.

[[speaker:sera]]“No. He struck here because this is where you would arrive first.”

Lei looked down.

A hair-thin metal filament had been buried inside the mortar.

Not an explosive.

A sensor.

Someone had measured the exact pressure of Lei's first response.

Sera pulled it free with tweezers.

[[speaker:sera]]“They did not come to break the gate.”

Lei's face darkened.

[[speaker:sera]]“They came to record the Duke who defended it.”

title: Rhen Says Yes
text:
They returned to the fortress after midnight.

Lei disappeared into a command meeting.

Sera found Rhen alone on the western wall.

He had been suspiciously quiet since the tea shop.

She stood beside him.

[[speaker:sera]]“You still haven't answered.”

Rhen looked at her.

[[speaker:rhen]]“I was attacked by a proposal.”

[[speaker:sera]]“You survived.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“Barely.”

Sera folded her arms.

He smiled.

Then the humor left his face.

[[speaker:rhen]]“Yes.”

Simple.

No speech.

No legend.

Just yes.

Sera looked away because suddenly the ruined northern landscape was easier to face than him.

Rhen reached for her hand.

She let him.

[[speaker:rhen]]“Was that proper enough?”

[[speaker:sera]]“No.”

He blinked.

Sera turned back.

[[speaker:sera]]“But I'll accept it.”

She kissed him again.

Slower this time.

When they separated, someone coughed behind them.

Lei Zhen stood ten paces away.

Sera closed her eyes.

[[speaker:lei]]“I can return later.”

[[speaker:sera]]“You can disappear forever.”

Lei almost smiled.

He had brought intelligence.

The Black Sun Host was not raiding randomly.

Its army moved in nine columns toward locations once used by the old anti-sovereign networks.

At the centre of every route was the same name.

Jiang Taixuan.

No public rank.

No modern sect.

No place in the Top Ten.

Lei had heard one rumor from the far north.

An unranked martial sovereign who had defeated every challenge offered to him, then refused to enter the ranking system because he considered it provincial.

Sera looked at Rhen.

[[speaker:sera]]“How strong?”

Rhen studied the map.

[[speaker:rhen]]“Strong enough that Lei should not assume the title is vanity.”

Lei said nothing.

That was warning enough.

Rhen eventually found words after Sera's proposal.

Too many.

He tried to explain that he had never expected to marry, had no idea what customs mattered, and suspected Haejin would make the process unbearable.

Sera listened for almost a minute.

Then put one finger against his lips.

[[speaker:sera]]“You already said yes.”

Rhen stopped.

[[speaker:sera]]“Everything after that is logistics.”

He laughed.

She took his hand and drew a tiny circle around his ring finger with one nail.

[[speaker:sera]]“Something simple.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“Agreed.”

[[speaker:sera]]“No giant jade.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“Agreed.”

[[speaker:sera]]“No ancient royal artifact.”

Rhen hesitated.

Sera narrowed her eyes.

[[speaker:rhen]]“Agreed.”

title: The Red Loom
text:
The second Black Sun commander arrived without an army.

Mi Suyun was not famous in the public rankings. Inside the Black Sun Host, however, she was the **Red Loom Strategist** — Jiang Taixuan's formation specialist, a woman who turned groups of ordinary soldiers into coordinated battlefield systems through timing networks rather than overwhelming personal strength.

Mi Suyun entered the fortress disguised as a grain clerk.

Sera found her because the woman counted doorways instead of people.

They met inside a storage hall.

Mi removed the clerk's cap.

Red cords were wound around both wrists.

[[speaker:mi]]“Pale Orchid.”

[[speaker:sera]]“You know me.”

[[speaker:mi]]“Jiang Taixuan knows everyone worth knowing.”

Sera disliked the sentence immediately.

Mi Suyun was known inside the Black Sun Host as the Red Loom Strategist.

Her martial art was **Battle Loom**.

She threaded thin qi filaments through prepared soldiers, not controlling them, but sharing timing information between units. A hundred mediocre fighters could respond like one experienced formation.

Sera drew one wire.

Mi drew ten.

The storage hall became a geometry problem with sharp consequences.

Sera cut the first line.

Mi replaced it.

Sera stepped inside Veiled Moon.

Mi abandoned sight and followed tension instead.

Interesting.

They fought for seven minutes without either landing a clean strike.

Then Sera noticed something.

Mi's right wrist always tightened before she changed the entire network.

Sera deliberately offered an opening.

Mi took it.

Silken Grave snapped around the support beam behind her.

The movement forced Mi to choose between maintaining Battle Loom and protecting her own arm.

She chose herself.

Sera's needle touched her throat.

[[speaker:sera]]“Found the person inside the formation.”

Mi smiled despite losing.

[[speaker:mi]]“That is why he wants to meet you.”

[[speaker:sera]]“He can make an appointment.”

Mi escaped by cutting her own red cords and dropping through a grain chute.

Sera let her go.

Not out of mercy.

She had attached a tracking thread to Mi's sleeve.

Rhen found Sera afterward.

[[speaker:rhen]]“You let her escape.”

[[speaker:sera]]“I let her lead.”

He kissed the top of her head.

[[speaker:rhen]]“Very attractive.”

Sera stared.

[[speaker:sera]]“You're getting bolder.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“Engaged.”

She laughed despite herself.

Mi's discarded red cords told Sera more than the fight had.

Each strand carried a different knot sequence. Logistics. Reinforcement. Retreat. Sacrifice.

Sera sat on the storage-room floor sorting them by tension marks.

Rhen brought a lantern.

[[speaker:rhen]]“You could sleep.”

[[speaker:sera]]“You could stop suggesting impossible things.”

One cord had been cut twice and retied.

Mi had altered Jiang's orders in the field.

Not blindly obedient, then.

Sera kept that strand separate.

[[speaker:sera]]“She has opinions.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“Dangerous.”

[[speaker:sera]]“Useful.”

Sera pocketed the cord.

If the Black Sun Host contained people capable of disagreeing with Jiang, the army was not as solid as its banners suggested.

title: Ninefold Ruin Body
text:
Mi's trail led to an abandoned quarry forty miles north.

Lei came personally.

Sera objected.

[[speaker:sera]]“If this is bait, sending #4 is generous.”

[[speaker:lei]]“If it is bait, I want to know what they think can close the trap.”

Rhen said nothing.

That made Sera more uneasy.

The quarry was empty except for one man.

Jiang Taixuan stood in plain black robes with no armor and no visible weapon.

He looked perhaps forty.

Broad-shouldered.

Silver at the temples.

His presence was strange.

Not explosive.

Dense.

As though the air had forgotten how to move around him.

[[speaker:jiang]]“Lei Zhen.”

Lei's thunder answered.

Jiang looked at Sera.

Then Rhen.

He paused for the smallest fraction of a breath.

Not recognition.

Instinct.

Something in him understood Rhen was wrong in a way the rankings could not describe.

But Jiang turned back to Lei.

[[speaker:jiang]]“Show me the Black Storm.”

Lei attacked.

The first bolt struck Jiang's chest.

He moved one step backward.

Only one.

Sera's eyes narrowed.

Jiang's cultivation was **Ninefold Ruin Body**.

Each internal layer accepted a portion of incoming force, changed its route, and stored part of the pressure across the next layer.

Not invulnerability.

Not absorption without limit.

But an extraordinarily efficient body-cultivation system built for surviving monsters.

Lei struck again.

Harder.

Jiang's second layer cracked.

He smiled.

[[speaker:jiang]]“Good.”

Then he crossed the distance and hit Lei once.

The quarry floor split.

Lei blocked.

Still slid twenty metres.

Rhen moved half a step.

Sera caught his sleeve.

[[speaker:sera]]“Lei is still fighting.”

Rhen stopped.

Lei looked furious.

And pleased.

For the first time in years, #4 had found an unranked man he could not dismiss.

After Jiang vanished from the quarry, Sera inspected the crater where Lei's strongest strike had landed.

The stone beneath it had nine concentric fracture lines.

Ninefold Ruin Body had not simply absorbed force inside Jiang.

He had bled portions of it through his feet and into the terrain.

Sera showed Lei.

[[speaker:lei]]“So I was hitting the quarry too.”

[[speaker:sera]]“Mostly the quarry.”

Lei looked offended.

Rhen crouched beside the fractures.

[[speaker:rhen]]“He cannot do that without contact.”

Sera understood.

Take away stable ground.

Take away anchors.

Make Jiang carry all of the punishment himself.

The first real weakness in the Uncrowned Emperor had appeared beneath their feet.

title: Black Storm, Uncrowned Emperor
text:
Lei and Jiang fought for twenty-six minutes.

The quarry ceased being a quarry.

Black thunder ripped through stone shelves.

Jiang's Ninefold Ruin Body broke layer after layer, then rebuilt circulation through deeper routes.

Lei changed frequency.

Jiang changed structure.

Neither man repeated the same exchange twice.

Sera watched from a fractured ridge.

She had seen Liang defeat Lei before.

This felt different.

Liang had controlled him.

Jiang endured him.

That distinction mattered tactically, not philosophically.

Jiang was not obviously above #4 in every category.

He was simply built to remain functional under punishment that would end most fights.

Lei eventually drove one lightning spear through Jiang's left shoulder.

Jiang answered with **Heaven-Burial Hand**.

A palm strike compressed force into a tiny contact point and disrupted the meridian route beneath the impact.

Lei blocked with his forearm.

The arm went numb instantly.

Sera moved.

Not to rescue him.

To destroy the prepared anchors surrounding the quarry.

She had finally seen them.

Mi Suyun's red cords were buried beneath the stone.

Jiang had been fighting inside a battlefield that fed timing data into his body.

Sera severed the first anchor.

Then the second.

Jiang felt it.

His eyes moved toward her.

That was enough.

Lei's thunder struck him cleanly and sent him through the quarry wall.

When the dust cleared, Jiang was gone.

Lei flexed his numb hand.

[[speaker:lei]]“Annoying.”

Rhen almost smiled.

Sera looked at the blood Jiang had left on the stone.

[[speaker:sera]]“He can be hurt.”

Lei nodded.

[[speaker:lei]]“Yes.”

Then his expression darkened.

[[speaker:lei]]“But if he had been trying to kill me instead of measure me, that fight would have been worse.”

Far to the east, a white court bell began ringing.

Liang Yue's territory had received a black-sun seal.

Lei refused treatment for his numb arm until Sera threatened to have Rhen do it without permission.

That worked.

Rhen touched two points near the elbow. Circulation returned almost immediately.

Lei flexed his fingers.

[[speaker:lei]]“Annoying.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“You have said that before.”

[[speaker:lei]]“Still true.”

Sera leaned against the wall, watching both men.

Lei's fight had changed her estimate. Jiang was not some vague northern myth. He could hurt a Duke in a clean exchange.

But he had also bled.

He had retreated when Sera removed his information advantage.

Powerful did not mean unknowable.

That distinction gave Sera something she trusted more than fear.

A problem.

title: White Court Warning
text:
Liang Yue answered the threat with one message.

COME.

Sera read it twice.

No fear.

No request for help.

Just invitation.

World Rank #2 had been the Bloodless Empress long before Sera knew her personally. Former World #1. A physician-killer whose control over circulation was so precise that she could stop armies without spilling blood.

Jiang Taixuan had chosen her next.

Lei wanted to go.

Liang refused him.

[[speaker:lei]]“She thinks I will interfere.”

Sera folded the letter.

[[speaker:sera]]“Would you?”

Lei said nothing.

Exactly.

Rhen remained quiet.

Sera looked at him.

[[speaker:sera]]“You are thinking too loudly.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“That seems impossible.”

[[speaker:sera]]“For you? No.”

He finally admitted the problem.

Jiang's Ninefold Ruin Body might be unusually well-suited against Liang.

Her techniques invaded circulation.

His entire cultivation was built around rerouting circulation under damage.

Not immunity.

A counter relationship.

Sera hated it.

[[speaker:sera]]“Then we warn her.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“She knows.”

Sera stood.

[[speaker:sera]]“Then I warn her again.”

Before leaving, she took Rhen by the collar and kissed him.

Lei looked away immediately.

[[speaker:sera]]“For luck.”

Rhen blinked.

[[speaker:rhen]]“Mine or yours?”

[[speaker:sera]]“Both.”

They rode east.

Behind them, Lei remained at the gate.

He had his own border to protect.

No convenient gathering of Dukes.

The Black Sun Host had learned to attack several territories at once.

The ride toward White Court grew quieter the farther east they went.

Sera finally asked Rhen the question that had been sitting between them.

[[speaker:sera]]“If Jiang beats Liang?”

Rhen did not answer immediately.

[[speaker:sera]]“I am not asking whether you can beat him.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“I know.”

She waited.

[[speaker:rhen]]“Then the ranking changes only if Liang chooses to make it public.”

Sera frowned.

[[speaker:rhen]]“Rank is an institution. Defeat is an event.”

She thought about that.

Then smiled faintly.

[[speaker:sera]]“You really hate rankings.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“They create paperwork.”

Sera laughed into the wind.

title: The Black Sun Host
text:
The road east revealed the true scale of Jiang's force.

Qiu Shen, called the **Hollow Ox**, was another Black Sun commander. A lower-Marquis-level body cultivator, he was built for one ugly military purpose: hold a road, bridge or gate against stronger opponents long enough for Jiang's army to keep moving.

Not hundreds.

Thousands.

Nine army columns moving independently beneath black sun banners.

Each column carried its own specialists, supply corps and formation anchors.

Sera counted what she could see.

Then doubled it.

[[speaker:sera]]“This is not a raid.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“No.”

[[speaker:sera]]“It's a campaign.”

They encountered the third commander at a river crossing.

Qiu Shen.

Known as the Hollow Ox.

A massive body cultivator around lower-Marquis territory whose job was not to defeat ranked monsters, but to hold bridges long enough for armies to move.

His technique, **Four-Pillar Frame**, locked his stance through four rotating chains of internal force.

Sera attacked the bridge supports instead.

Qiu laughed.

[[speaker:qiu]]“Pale Orchid fights wood now?”

[[speaker:sera]]“Only when wood is more important than you.”

The bridge tilted.

His stance remained perfect.

The ground beneath it did not.

Qiu had to choose between holding his formation and falling into the river with it.

He jumped.

Rhen caught Sera around the waist as the bridge collapsed.

She looked down at his arm.

Then at him.

[[speaker:sera]]“Convenient.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“Engagement privilege.”

Sera smiled.

[[speaker:sera]]“Approved.”

They crossed by rope while the Black Sun column rerouted upstream.

Sera had delayed an army without fighting the army.

By evening they reached White Court territory.

Every gate was open.

Liang Yue was waiting alone.

At the river crossing, Qiu Shen did not simply vanish after the bridge fell.

He surfaced downstream clinging to one broken beam, furious but alive.

Sera threw him a rope.

Qiu stared at it.

[[speaker:qiu]]“Why?”

[[speaker:sera]]“Because drowning you teaches me nothing.”

He climbed out slowly.

Rhen watched from the opposite bank.

Qiu looked between them.

[[speaker:qiu]]“You two are strange.”

[[speaker:sera]]“Frequently.”

Before leaving, Qiu warned her that Jiang's loyal core did not fear Dukes.

Sera tightened the rope around her pack.

[[speaker:sera]]“Everyone fears something.”

Qiu smiled bitterly.

[[speaker:qiu]]“Then find his.”

title: Liang Yue Waits
text:
Liang stood in the central courtyard wearing white.

Liang Yue was waiting in white.

**World Rank #2, Duchess of the White Court — the Bloodless Empress.** She had once been World #1 before Kael surpassed her, and her terrifying White Blood arts could control or stop circulation with physician-like precision. She was also one of the very few people alive who could speak to Rhen without treating him like a myth.

No armor.

No weapon.

Sera disliked that immediately.

[[speaker:sera]]“You intend to fight him alone.”

[[speaker:liang]]“Yes.”

[[speaker:sera]]“No.”

Liang looked at her.

Few people told World Rank #2 no.

Sera had become one of them.

Rhen examined the courtyard.

Liang noticed.

[[speaker:liang]]“Do not interfere.”

Rhen met her eyes.

[[speaker:rhen]]“If you are dying, I will.”

Liang accepted that because arguing would be pointless.

Sera spent the night searching the estate for anchors.

She found none.

That worried her more.

Jiang was not preparing the same battlefield.

He intended to fight Liang differently.

Before dawn, Liang joined Sera on the veranda.

[[speaker:liang]]“You are engaged.”

Sera almost dropped her tea.

[[speaker:sera]]“How do you know?”

Liang looked toward Rhen sleeping against a pillar with Sera's coat over him.

[[speaker:liang]]“I am a physician.”

Sera stared.

[[speaker:liang]]“Also Haejin sent a letter.”

Sera closed her eyes.

Of course she had.

Liang's mouth moved almost imperceptibly.

A smile.

[[speaker:liang]]“Congratulations.”

For one quiet minute, there was no war.

Then the outer bell rang once.

A man in black walked through the open gate.

Jiang Taixuan had arrived.

Liang's estate felt different from the northern fortress.

Quiet.

White stone.

No visible weapons.

Every servant moved with medical precision.

Sera remembered the first time Liang's presence had frightened her more than armies.

Now she saw the woman beneath the title more clearly.

Liang poured tea herself.

[[speaker:liang]]“You are staring.”

[[speaker:sera]]“Thinking.”

[[speaker:liang]]“Dangerous.”

Sera smiled.

[[speaker:sera]]“Rhen says that too.”

Liang's eyes moved briefly toward him.

[[speaker:liang]]“He is correct occasionally.”

Rhen looked offended.

For one small moment, three people with enough history to terrify nations simply argued over tea quality.

title: The White Court Bell
text:
Jiang stopped twenty paces from Liang.

He bowed.

Not mockingly.

[[speaker:jiang]]“Former World #1.”

Liang's expression did not change.

[[speaker:liang]]“Unranked.”

Jiang smiled.

[[speaker:jiang]]“Precisely.”

Sera stood beneath the eastern eaves.

Rhen beside her.

Neither moved.

This belonged to Liang until it did not.

The first exchange made no sound.

Liang touched Jiang's wrist.

His right hand stopped.

Jiang rotated the second layer of Ninefold Ruin Body.

The hand moved again.

Liang's eyes sharpened.

White Blood entered his circulation from three points.

Jiang broke one route, redirected another, and accepted the third long enough to step inside her reach.

Heaven-Burial Hand struck.

Liang turned.

The palm missed her heart by inches.

The courtyard wall behind her collapsed.

Sera's fingers tightened around her wire.

Rhen remained still.

The second exchange lasted longer.

Then the third.

By sunset, half the White Court courtyard was gone.

Liang had blood on one sleeve.

Jiang had blood at his mouth.

Neither had yielded.

Sera finally understood why the northern archive had opened.

This was not merely an invasion.

A new sovereign had come south to test the entire hierarchy.

Jiang wiped blood from his chin.

[[speaker:jiang]]“Again.”

Liang raised one hand.

White qi gathered around her fingers.

[[speaker:liang]]“Gladly.”

The White Court bell rang for the second time.

When the second White Court bell rang, servants closed every outer door.

Not to trap Jiang.

To keep everyone else out.

Liang had ordered the courtyard cleared long before his arrival.

Sera realized she had prepared for defeat as carefully as victory.

Medical teams waited underground.

Escape corridors were open.

No civilian stood behind the walls Jiang might break.

Sera respected that.

Jiang did too.

[[speaker:jiang]]“You removed every hostage.”

Liang raised her hand.

[[speaker:liang]]“I dislike clutter.”

The answer was so dry that even Sera almost laughed.

Then White Blood moved.

The courtyard stopped being a place for conversation.
